Major Ion Chemistry

Source: R/geochemistry.R
major_ion_chemistry.Rd

Extracts, standardizes, and converts major-ion chemistry data for hydrogeochemical analysis.

Usage

major_ion_chemistry(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
major_ion_chemistry(df, location, analyte, result, unit, sample_date, ...)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
major_ion_chemistry(
  df,
  analytes = c("Calcium, dissolved", "Magnesium, dissolved", "Sodium, dissolved",
    "Potassium, dissolved", "Chloride, total", "Sulfate, total",
    "Alkalinity, total (lab)"),
  analyte_matching = c("exact", "strict", "normalized"),
  ...
)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location

Location identifier column.

analyte

Analyte column.

result

Analytical result column.

unit

Reporting unit column.

sample_date

Sample date column.

analytes

Major-ion analytes to retain.

analyte_matching

Analyte matching strategy. One of `"exact"`, `"strict"`, or `"normalized"`.

Value

An `env_schema` object containing standardized major-ion chemistry data.

Details

`major_ion_chemistry()` is an S3 generic that supports both raw data frames and `env_schema` objects.

For data frames, environmental column mappings must be supplied. For `env_schema` objects, mapped schema fields are used automatically.

Major-ion analytes are standardized, duplicate measurements are consolidated, and analytical results are converted to milliequivalents per liter (meq/L).

For data frames, `major_ion_chemistry()` first converts the supplied data to an `env_schema` object using the specified column mappings and then dispatches to [major_ion_chemistry.env_schema()].

`major_ion_chemistry()` serves as the primary preprocessing function for geochemical analyses and diagrams.

The function:

  • resolves analyte names;

  • filters requested analytes;

  • consolidates duplicate measurements;

  • standardizes analytical metadata;

  • converts concentrations to milliequivalents per liter (meq/L).

Duplicate measurements within a location and sample-date combination are averaged prior to conversion.

Analyte Matching

exact

Uses analyte names exactly as reported.

strict

Applies text normalization while preserving analytical distinctions such as dissolved versus total fractions.

normalized

Resolves analyte aliases to canonical analyte names using package analyte metadata.

Output Structure

One record is returned for each unique analyte, location, and sample-date combination.

Analytical concentrations are available in both native units and standardized milliequivalent units suitable for geochemical calculations.

Examples

data(gw)

chem <- major_ion_chemistry(gw)

chem

#>    location_id sample_date         analyte      .analyte_id .original_lab_result

#>  1 MW-1        2007-12-20 00:00:00 Bicarbonate… bicarbonate               179

#>  3 MW-1        2007-12-20 00:00:00 Chloride, t… chloride                   30   
#>  4 MW-1        2007-12-20 00:00:00 Magnesium, … magnesium                  21   
#>  5 MW-1        2007-12-20 00:00:00 Potassium, … potassium                   3.25
#>  6 MW-1        2007-12-20 00:00:00 Sodium, dis… sodium                     17.9

#> 10 MW-1        2008-02-20 00:00:00 Chloride, t… chloride                   25
